post.caption:
Skeletons from the first farming societies are shorter and show more disease than the hunter-gatherers before them. Narrower diets, denser living alongside livestock, harder labour and much worse teeth. Surplus also enabled permanent settlement, specialisation, hierarchy and writing. Agriculture was a great deal for the species and a bad deal for the average individual, for thousands of years. That tension is the whole story.
